lines.text: Meet sind. Slurm in Docker.
Real Slurm clusters, in Docker containers, right on your machine.
For development, tests and CI, from the terminal or the browser.
Install it with meez. Docker is the only thing you need.
Then sind doctor checks that the host is ready.
Describe a cluster in YAML, and create it with one command.
Now you see your clusters and their nodes.
sind enter opens a shell on the submitter.
Your working directory on the host is the data directory on every node.
Submit jobs, and watch the queue.
The database node keeps the job accounting.
Or run a single command, straight from the host.
sind ssh reaches any node.
sind publishes no ports. A relay on the mesh carries the SSH connection.
Or use your own ssh. Just include the config that sind writes.
Then ssh and scp reach each node by name.
Port forwards reach the services on the nodes.
With systemd resolve-dee, your host finds each node by name, too.
Follow the logs of a container, or of a single service, live.
Add workers to a running cluster.
Simulate failures. Freeze, cut, or reboot nodes.
Slurm marks the frozen node as not responding.
Node expressions select many nodes at once.
And remove workers when you're done.
slurmrestd serves the REST API on the api node, with JWT.
Users, groups and Slurm accounts come straight from the config.
A backup controller takes over,
when the primary controller fails.
Turn on monitoring, and each realm gets Prometheus, Loki and Grafana.
Grafana shows the Slurm dashboards of your cluster.
The images ship current Slurm releases for amd64 and arm64, with CVMFS on request.
A realm keeps its clusters apart, for parallel work and CI.
Connect other containers, like kind nodes, to the realm's networks.
sind ui opens in your browser, and only you can open it.
The overview shows all realms, clusters and nodes, live.
A new cluster is a form, a plan, and the exact command.
First, a name. Let's call it lab.
Tick a box to add a node, like the api node for the REST API. The plan on the right follows every change.
Then set how many workers you want. Three, this time.
Slurm config takes your own lines for slurm dot conf and its friends. sind writes them after its own.
Edit YAML opens the whole config. The form waits until you discard your edits.
Create saves the config, and runs the very command the plan shows.
Watch each step and each node, as it happens.
When a run fails, sind ui tells you why, and what to do.
Here's the health of each service, on each node.
Select nodes as a node set, then power them.
Logs, from a container or one service, followed live.
Connect shows the ssh and exec commands, ready to copy.
There's mesh and DNS, topology, monitoring and doctor.
Press slash to jump to any node or page, and question mark for help.
Light, or dark.
In CI, it's one step with the sind action.
Plain progress lines and a JSON event log suit CI and scripts.
When you're done, delete everything with one command.
That's sind. Find the docs and the code at these links.
